title: Burma
capsule: Burma (Myanmar) in the dataset period (1820–1990) spans the final decades of the Konbaung dynasty—which clashed with British India in three Anglo-Burmese Wars (1824–26, 1852, 1885), culminating in the annexation of the kingdom and exile of King Thibaw Min—through the colonial period (1885–1948), independence, and the socialist era under Ne Win (coup 1962) until the military's formal reconstitution of the state as Myanmar in 1989. The Second Anglo-Burmese War (1852) cost Burma its entire coastal littoral, and the third (1885) extinguished the monarchy entirely. Ne Win's Burma Socialist Programme Party ruled until 1988, when student protests and a second coup brought the State Law and Order Restoration Council to power, which renamed the country Myanmar in 1989.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Burma's colonial-era boundaries were defined by British administrative surveys and treaties with neighboring powers (China, Siam, France for Indochina); they are generally well-attested, though hill-tribe frontier zones were loosely administered.
